Wait until no jobs are running.

## Synopsis

```text
wait [jobid=<jobid>] [jobname=<jobname>] [job=<job>] [ujobid=<ujobid>] [mount]
     [timeout=<timeout>] [catalog=<catalog>]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Blocks the session until jobs have finished. Without an argument it waits until no job is running. With jobid=, jobname= or job= (a prefix of a running job's name suffices) or ujobid= it waits for that one job and then prints JobId and JobStatus; a JobId that is not running is looked up in the catalog at once. Only the first such argument counts.

With mount the command waits until a running job asks for a volume or a mount; timeout= limits that wait in seconds. Nothing is changed. The command is meant for scripts, for example after run ... yes and before evaluating the result.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobid=` | integer |  |  |  | Job ID. |
| `jobname=` | string |  |  |  | Running job name prefix. |
| `job=` | string |  |  |  | Same as jobname=. |
| `ujobid=` | string |  |  |  | Unique running job name. |
| `mount` | keyword |  |  |  | Wait for a media or mount request. |
| `timeout=` | integer |  |  |  | Mount wait timeout in seconds. |
| `catalog=` | resource | from [`.catalogs`](../dot-catalogs/) |  |  | Catalog name. |

## Examples

Return when no job is running any more:

```text
wait
```

Wait for job 42 and print its final status:

```text
wait jobid=42
```

Wait up to five minutes for a mount request:

```text
wait mount timeout=300
```
